algorithm: Explicit Euler integration of logistic growth
data_flow_ascii:
PARAMS (r, K, P0) + --steps/--dt -> simulate (Euler loop)
trajectory rows -> print_trajectory (sampled table)
rows -> start/end/peak summary
description_sentence: Euler-integrates logistic growth dP/dt = r*P*(1-P/K) and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.
failure_note: A non-positive carrying capacity K would flip the growth sign; the template documents K as positive and the default params keep it well-behaved.

functions.desc: Euler-integrate logistic growth; return [(t, value)] rows.
functions.name: simulate

functions.desc: Print every Nth trajectory row plus the final state.
functions.name: print_trajectory

functions.desc: Parse args, simulate, and print the trajectory and summary.
functions.name: main

label: Simulation (logistic growth)
output_shape: A sampled trajectory table (t, value) plus start, end, peak, and carrying-capacity summary lines.
pitch_sentence: A {topic} simulation in pure Python that integrates logistic growth with Euler steps and prints the full trajectory toward carrying capacity.

qa.a: Logistic growth: fast early rise that levels off at the carrying capacity K, a common shape for adoption and saturation processes.
qa.q: What dynamics does the model show?

qa.a: --steps and --dt; smaller dt is more accurate, larger dt runs faster but can overshoot.
Euler is first-order and simple to read; the template favors clarity over the accuracy of higher-order integrators.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} simulator in Python (stdlib) implementing Euler integration of logistic growth with seeded parameters; demo runs end-to-end and prints the trajectory table with summary statistics.
scaling_note: The trajectory is a plain list, so millions of steps would use noticeable memory; streaming or downsampling would fix that.
storage_note: In-memory only: the trajectory list exists for the run and is not persisted.
tradeoff_note: Explicit Euler is the simplest integrator to read and verify, at the cost of accuracy versus higher-order methods for stiff dynamics.
